original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.

Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.

actual_scope: After one scalar elimination, does the filled Schur complement of the narrow banded witness remain bandwidth b, or only its inverse?
scope_change_reason: The circular-section bound is already packaged. The note's next unresolved sentence is the Schur step: inverse bounds are claimed for the complement, while bandwidth b is proved only for principal sections.
bottleneck_link: Iterated elimination in the narrow conditioning argument reuses the inverse bound. Reusing the bandwidth count on a filled complement would be a different implication, and this witness separates the two.
stop_rule: Stop at one explicit scalar elimination. Do not audit the Gaussian tail or a boundary-order block factorization.
evidence: research/schur-bandwidth-gap exhibits a bandwidth-2 matrix whose Schur complement has bandwidth 3, while the inverse of that complement remains inside the original Neumann bounds.
